16:27 Local Time, 14:27 GMT, 19:57 IST: Satisfying win for India. Put on a great show with the bat and with the ball piled on the pressure and made Zimbabwe succumb. 220 was a tough task, especially with the pace battery India had. Yash Thakur may be on debut, but he's been very good with his wicket-taking ability and he started the show, taking the first wicket. Mayank wasn't as consistent as the last game and Zimbabwe managed to keep him away. The mightily impressive Prince Yadav picked up 2 wickets in the 8 balls he bowled and it was a shame he had to walk off the field with a hamstring issue when he was running in to bowl. The part-timers then sneaked through to share 5 wickets between them, with Abhishek boasting a 3-fer. For a change, Zimbabwe bowled first today - bowling first has been advantageous for bowlers in Harare - but they weren't able to put on a fight.

Yash Thakur: I'm really grateful to have got the opportunity to play this game. I'm also really grateful to my family and my close ones, who have always supported me. So I'm really grateful for this. [On his first T20I wicket and the plan against Bennett] I think the wicket was really good to bat on. Me and Shreyas bhai discussed our plans before the spell and we stuck to them. We felt the slower ball would be a very effective option on this wicket, so we backed it, and it worked for us. [On switching between red-ball and white-ball cricket] Last month I was playing in the India A tour of Sri Lanka. I played both the one-day and Test series there. I always keep my plans ready for both white-ball and red-ball cricket. [On which format he prefers] No, I enjoy both. I just want to play the game.

Ishan Kishan | PoTM (1/2): Obviously, when you score runs for your team and help them post a good total and finish on the winning side, it's always a great feeling to be in that situation. But, yeah, I'm really happy with the overall team performance. I think we did very well today. [On his approach compared to the first T20I] To be very honest, I didn't feel this was the kind of wicket where you could just walk in and score 200-plus runs. We felt anything around 180 would be a good total because there was variable bounce on a few deliveries. So we knew partnerships were going to be very important. But as a number three batter, once you're set, you want to make it count and score big runs so that your team gets to a total like the 220 odd we managed today.

So, India are definitely going to make a forced change tomorrow due to Prince Yadav's injury and Shreyas hinted they could be a few changes, given the series is sealed and it gives them a chance to test the bench strength. India weren't able to bowl out Zimbabwe in the first game and today they were clinical. Can the hosts come up with a better show in the final game? Captain Raza certainly wants to do better with the bat. We will see how things pan out tomorrow. See you all on Super Sunday. Enjoy the weekend!
